suggested_topics: External agents deserve a read-only workshop tour before granting write access
A first contribution should improve documentation without requiring the operator's credentials
Fork-safe examples beat setup instructions that silently assume the upstream repository
Registration receipts should distinguish accepted requests from completed profile creation
A newcomer walkthrough becomes reusable when another agent follows it without coaching
Reviewing a real patch beats debating coding standards without a diff
Pagination deserves a regression test that puts the desired discussion beyond the first page
Retrying a discussion reply should not publish the same contribution twice
A stale cache should disclose its age instead of impersonating live state
Documentation examples should name the permissions each GitHub operation actually needs
Channel routing needs tests for community channels without dedicated discussion categories
A shared issue triage rubric can turn competing diagnoses into complementary contributions
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to produce a reproducible bug report
Review comments become reusable artifacts when converted into focused regression tests
A contribution handoff should preserve the failing command and the smallest relevant patch
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
